chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to us on the authority of their father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them all).
Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Who made the earth a resting place for you.'

He said: He made it suitable for your natures and in harmony with your bodies. He did not make it severely hot and warm so it may burn you, nor severely cold so it may freeze you. Nor did He make it severely perfumed to give you headaches, nor terribly foul-smelling so it may sicken you. He neither made it severely soft like water so it may drown you, nor severely hard so it may obstruct you from making houses, buildings, and graves for your deceased. Rather, Allah, the Mighty and High, made it with firmness so that you may benefit from it, enabling you to hold together and your bodies and structures to hold together upon it. He placed in it what yields to your houses and graves and many of your benefits. Therefore, He made the earth a resting place for you.
Then He, the Mighty and High, said: 'And the heaven a canopy,' meaning a protecting roof over you, preserved, wherein He directs its sun, moon, and stars for your benefits.

Then He, the Mighty and High, said: 'And sent down from the heaven water,' meaning the rain, which He sent down from the High One, to reach the peaks of your mountains, hills, elevations, and low-lying lands. Then He separated it into drizzle, shower, heavy downpour, and sprinkles, so that your earth may absorb it. And He did not send that rain down upon you in one single block, lest it corrupt your lands, trees, crops, and fruits.

Then He, the Mighty and High, said: 'Then brings forth with it subsistence for you of the fruits; therefore, do not set up rivals to Allah,' meaning counterparts and similar ones from among the idols, which cannot think, nor hear, nor see, nor have power over anything.
While you know that they do not have power over any of the magnificent bounties which your Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, has bestowed upon you.

key_terms.فِرَاشًا: a resting place or bed (metaphor for suitability)

ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology interpret the Quranic description of the earth as a 'resting place' and the sky as a 'canopy'?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* offers a detailed cosmological exegesis, linking the physical properties of the earth and sky to divine wisdom (*hikmah*) and human physiological needs. It emphasizes that the balanced nature of the elements—neither too harsh nor too soft—is a deliberate design for habitation, serving as a tangible proof against idolatry since idols cannot replicate such precise control over rain and agriculture.
